Warsaw Airports Resume Operations After Security Alerts on London and Copenhagen Flights

03 Nov 2026, 05:02 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

2 min read

Key takeawaysWarsaw Modlin Airport has partially resumed operations following an earlier bomb threat reported on a London flight, according to airport statements. Security forces continue to inspect the specific section where the aircraft was parked.

Airport Operations Resume Following Security Threats

Warsaw Modlin Airport has partially resumed operations following an earlier bomb threat reported on a London flight, according to airport statements. Security forces continue to inspect the specific section where the aircraft was parked.

Reported details concerning the incident include:

  • A flight arriving from London Heathrow made an unplanned landing at Modlin Airport following a security alert.
  • Passengers have been allowed to disembark to the main terminal while emergency procedures continue.
  • Airport authorities stated that further actions are being carried out according to standard safety protocols.

Additionally, media reports from Denmark indicate a separate security threat involving an SAS flight from Copenhagen to Warsaw, which also prompted deployment of security teams and sniffer dogs for assessment.

Diplomatic Talks and Regional Developments

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Berlin for unexpected discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and President Frank-Walter Steinmeier. According to reported statements, the meetings focus on diplomatic coordination, air defense, and the energy sector ahead of upcoming US-mediated talks.

The Kremlin confirmed that trilateral discussions involving Russia, Ukraine, and the United States are scheduled to take place in Abu Dhabi next week.

For official updates regarding airport status, travelers and observers should consult:

  • Direct statements from Warsaw Modlin Airport and Polish aviation authorities.
  • Official announcements from relevant European transport ministries and law enforcement agencies.
  • Verified updates from established news organizations covering ongoing European transport and diplomatic events.
